In the CS2 console, no password. Or find Over Strike 2 in the community server browser.

Over the top – On the Huis

The menu Everything is a click: hold TAB for the board, TAB + E for the full menu. Every action has a chat command too: !help lists them.

Queue

Queue
Who is next – least play time goes first
Cancel
Drop one of your requests, or all of them
I’m done
End your own map: the queue moves on
Vote to skip
Someone else’s map: a majority of the others skips it

Voting

Like Dislike
On the map that is on – the same again undoes it
Too big
A dislike: only 1 random pick in 100 is a too-big map beside Like and Dislike, and Big on every map card; it marks the map too big
Ads
A dislike for ads or a server redirect: never a random pick beside Too big, and on every map card; anybody can still pick the map
Maps›arrows
Vote on any map’s card: up likes it, down dislikes it
Sort›Votes
The most liked maps first

Game

Grenade drops
On or off, for everyone back on after 10 minutes with nobody on
Match length
10 or 60 minutes, from the next match
New maps
Always the new maps, Half a coin flip, Never the original list where random picks come from, for everyone: the new maps are #1017 and up, the original list #1–#1016
Restart
Reboot a stuck server – click twice to confirm the whole server, not the match
Fun
Friendly fire, low gravity and more, until the map changes sixteen settings anybody switches for everyone, and the news line says who; friendly fire, Instakill and Grenades x10 start every map on

This page: the rules and the maps

Random maps

When a match ends everybody votes for the next map: 5 maps and Random, for 60 s or until a majority agrees; your queued map is on it with your vote in.

Random maps - at start, and when nobody votes - are biased by Workshop popularity and by the votes.

How voting counts

Each upvote doubles a map's odds on the dice (max 5), each downvote quarters them, Workshop rank gives up to 3x.

One vote per player per map, and it is kept.

Fair queue

  • Whoever has had the least play time on their own requests goes next, so one player's five requests wait behind everyone else's first.
  • A map two or more players asked for goes first.
  • A requested map stays until its match ends, its requester clicks I’m done, a skip vote passes, or the requester has been gone over a minute while others wait.
  • Up to 5 requests each, and only while you're on the server.

How it works Every chance in picking a map, word for word as the menu’s How it works page has it.

Picking a map

  • Play on a card is a request. On a map nobody holds it plays at once; on somebody's map it waits in the queue.
  • The queue: a map two or more players asked for goes first, then whoever has had the least play time on their own requests.
  • A requested map stays until its match ends, its requester clicks I'm done, a skip vote passes, or the requester has been gone over a minute while others wait.
  • Up to 5 requests each, only while you're on the server. Previous asks for the map before this one.

Next and random maps

  • Next rolls a random map when nobody holds this one; on your own map it is I'm done, on somebody else's a vote to skip.
  • When a match ends everybody votes for 60 s, or until a majority agrees: 5 maps and Random. A queued map is on the ballot with its requesters' votes in.
  • Each other mode gets a map on it: Deathmatch, and Wingman up to 4 players. Ties are drawn; no votes is Random. Arms Race after 10 minutes with nobody on.
  • The server rolls one at start. The vote's map stays until its match ends or a skip vote passes. A map a player picked or queued is never random.

Which maps a random pick takes

  • The New maps setting (Game page, anybody): Always - the new maps, #1017 and up. Half - a coin flip per pick. Never - the original #1-#1016.
  • A list with nothing left to roll hands the pick to the other list, and the news line says so. 10 minutes with nobody on: back to Always.
  • 1 random pick in 100 takes a too-big map (measured XL, or marked Too big by a player), the other 99 one that is not; an empty group hands the pick to the other.

Weights and votes

  • Inside that group, Workshop rank gives up to 3x, each Like doubles a map's odds (up to 5 Likes), each Dislike or Too big quarters them.
  • One vote per player per map, kept: Like, or Dislike with a reason. Only Too big and Ads do more than a Dislike. The same button again takes it back.
  • Nothing else counts: a map's download size never makes it more or less likely.

Never rolled

  • The map that is on, and the last 10 maps played (while others are left).
  • Maps that crashed the server or are on the broken list, blocked maps, and maps gone from the Workshop.
  • Maps a player marked Ads (they show ads or send players to another server) - anybody can still pick them.

The maps

The 1,000 most-subscribed Arms Race maps on the Steam Workshop, plus 16 hand-picked glass maps and 2,678 more Arms Race maps, that actually load in Counter-Strike 2. Every ID verified live against Valve's API. In the game it all happens in the menu: hold TAB and press E, then find a map by its number here, its name or its tags, and click Play. Or copy a map's Workshop ID here and paste it into the game chat: the menu opens on that map. Running your own server? Flip Console in the toolbar for the host_workshop_map command instead.

First time on a map?

The server downloads a map the first time anyone picks it, so a 500 MB one takes a minute. After that it stays cached and switches instantly.

Maps that crash it

58 maps on this list are flagged for crashing or freezing the server — a red banner says what the test saw, and picking one in the game’s menu asks you to confirm before it switches.

4 maps were removed from the Workshop — nobody can download them, so the server refuses them; it checks the Workshop daily.

Every map on the list was load-tested on the server on 2026-10-03; no banner means it loaded. If one still takes the server down, it restarts by itself within a minute and the screen says which map did it.

Ranked by current subscriber count, which measures general popularity rather than fitness for Arms Race — the aim maps at the top are used for solo warmup by people who never touch the mode, while purpose-built ar_ maps sit far lower. At four players, physical size matters more than rank: Arms Race forces mp_randomspawn 1, so on a full defusal-sized map everyone spawns far apart and the ladder never advances. Filter to <25 MB for a session that keeps moving.

Every entry returned result=1, consumer_app_id=730 and an empty filename field from ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails. That last check is what matters: CS:GO-era uploads return mymaps/<name>.bsp and will not load in CS2, and several of them outrank the real maps in Steam search — including a 1.08M-subscriber “Aim Map” that is not the one in this list. Screenshots are the authors' own, mirrored from Valve's CDN.
